boundary_decision.rationale: Research Study aggregates protocol intent, evidence lineage and bounded findings under study-scoped authority; all external masters (project, participant, specimen, observation, dataset, publication, ethics, audit) deliberately retain independent identity and lifecycle authority. Consistent with Frascati (SRC-001), DDI Lifecycle (SRC-002, SRC-003), WHO TRDS (SRC-004), ClinicalTrials.gov (SRC-005), PROV (SRC-007) and DataCite (SRC-009, SRC-010). Frozen registry value 'standalone-mm' classifies record plane, not subject-model kind; aggregate is defensible schema choice.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root and Research Study entry kind
decisions.rationale: Research Study owns identity, lineage, protocol, design, conduct, evidence and findings as versioned inquiry aggregate; all external masters (project, participant, specimen, observation, dataset, publication, ethics, audit) remain deliberately external with independent lifecycle authority preserved. Boundary notes distinguish study from project (objectives and funding vs. inquiry and evidence), from experiment or trial (contained conduct vs. broader design), from participant or specimen (scoped eligibility vs. external master identity), from observation or dataset (study-scoped binding vs. data-product semantics), from publication (bounded findings vs. authored dissemination) and from ethics decision (study-scoped binding vs. independent oversight). Consistent with Frascati and clinical research governance standards (SRC-001, SRC-004, SRC-005).

All 16 sources declared primary authority_tier 1 with pinned versions, dates and accessible URLs. Governance includes Frascati 2015 (OECD standard for R&D classification), DDI Lifecycle 3.3 (data collection and maintainable structures), WHO TRDS 1.3.1 and ClinicalTrials.gov current (protocol registration), OGC OMS and ISO 19156:2023 (observation and measurement), W3C PROV, DCAT 3, RFC 3339 (provenance, discovery, timestamps), DataCite 4.6/4.7 (metadata and output identification), NIH DMS Policy (data sharing), NIH Privacy Best Practices (de-identification), NIST Privacy Framework (privacy governance), 45 CFR Part 46 (human subjects protection), UK National Archives (retention and disposal). DataCite 4.6/4.7 reconciliation already explicitly flagged in known_omissions; defer delta review to relation-approval phase. All source references remain live and verifiable.

decisions.concept: Composition relations and external master autonomy
decisions.rationale: No approved relation rows were supplied. Parent and reference relations to external masters, including research project, grant or award, experiment, trial, test execution, person, participant, population, sample, specimen, site, resource, instrument, observation, measurement, dataset, software, publication, ethics decision, artifact and audit record, are explicitly held as composition gaps pending relation definitions and approval. Service policies declare that study ownership does not transfer to linked masters and study disposition never cascades to linked masters. This is appropriate for a reviewable draft and preserves independent master identity, authority and lifecycle. Composition completeness cannot be claimed until relations are bound and reviewed.

Service layers properly separate study master from implementation systems and enforcement. Access default rule denies direct participant identifiers, sensitive attributes, consent records, confidential sponsor material, protected locations, unpublished hypotheses, embargoed outputs and raw evidence unless purpose-bound Dimension policy permits minimum necessary view. Roles and responsibilities explicitly distributed (sponsor, principal investigator, protocol steward, ethics body, data steward, reviewer, privacy and records steward). CRUD operations distinguish create (bind study and pre-conduct governance), update (append lifecycle, conduct, observation, analysis and finding events), delete (apply ethics, retention, participant-rights and legal-hold policy). Agent bootstrap, idempotency, preconditions, dry-run and post-check requirements are explicit. This governance framework is sound and consistent with research integrity, participant protection and records-management standards (SRC-005, SRC-011, SRC-012, SRC-013, SRC-014, SRC-015).

Five adversarial checks defend against critical failures. First, reject a study without stable identity, explicit questions or purpose, pinned protocol and design, accountable authority and evidence lineage. Second, reject consent inferred from enrolment, hypothesis support from significance, causality from association, generalizability from sample size or reproducibility from one study. Third, reject an amendment or correction that overwrites released questions, eligibility, sampling, outcomes, conduct, observations, analyses, findings or publications. Fourth, reject copied participant, specimen, observation, dataset, publication, ethics or project masters whose independent identity and lifecycle are lost. Fifth, reject agent contact, intervention assignment, protected disclosure, scientific signoff or disposition outside delegated authority and applicable policy controls. These checks are source-grounded in SRC-001, SRC-005, SRC-007, SRC-013 and SRC-014 and remain non-negotiable.

Model is cross-disciplinary kernel anchored on clinical and statistical R&D sources (OECD Frascati, DDI, WHO, ClinicalTrials.gov, NIST). Service-layer documentation explicitly notes: Human-subject, animal, environmental, export-control, privacy, intellectual-property, clinical, research-integrity and records obligations vary by jurisdiction, institution and discipline. OECD Frascati supplies statistical R&D boundary, not universal operational lifecycle. DDI strongest for social, behavioural, economic data; WHO and ClinicalTrials.gov are clinical-trial profiles; OMS observation-oriented; DCAT and DataCite focus discovery. 45 CFR Part 46 applies within US regulatory context only. Discipline-specific profiles (behavioral sciences, environmental sciences, biomedical research, social research, engineering, computer science) and regional variants (non-OECD contexts, non-US regulatory frameworks) must define their own ethics, privacy, consent, retention and disclosure policies before canonical deployment. Do not claim universal applicability.

deferred_research: Relation definitions and composition mappings: Explicit typed relations to external masters must be formalized with identity strategy, ownership, lifecycle linkage rules and no-cascade semantics. Candidate registry and composition rows remain unapproved and need steward review.

DataCite 4.6/4.7 interoperability reconciliation: The property-level mapping is pinned to DataCite Metadata Schema 4.6 while the official release history lists version 4.7 as current from 3 March 2026. Reconcile property and cardinality deltas, map relevant changes, verify round-trip fidelity and test the crosswalk with real registry records before canonical promotion.

Discipline-specific and regional profile variants: Clinical research (ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO TRDS, FDA IND/IDE), statistical R&D (Frascati), behavioral sciences, environmental sciences, biomedical research, social research, engineering and computer science each require discipline-specific protocol, ethics, privacy, consent and retention profiles. US regulatory context (45 CFR Part 46, FDA, HIPAA, NIH DMS) must be separated from European (GDPR, EMA, national ethics boards), international (World Bank, UNICEF), non-OECD and non-English-speaking contexts. Governance policies must be regionalized and require local ethics and legal review.

Agent operation policies and implementations: AGENTS.md bootstrap structure is defined (Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL, Processes URL) but no concrete agent implementations, delegation authorities, idempotency keys, preconditions, dry-run mode, expected-revision assertions or post-condition verifications are supplied. Separate agent-operation specification required before access, sharing, retention and disposition operations can be delegated to agents. Audit trail and tamper-evidence requirements must be explicit.

Bidirectional relation verification and master-side study discovery: No reverse mappings provided from external masters (project, experiment, participant, dataset, publication, ethics decision) back to study aggregate. Must verify that study identity is resolvable from external master references and that bidirectional links preserve both study and master autonomy. Cross-system consistency checks and conflict-resolution rules for competing assertions must be defined.

These variants are out of scope. Cannot claim universal applicability or cross-jurisdictional compliance.
